headline: Shift Data Center Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for their own grid infrastructure expansion costs, preventing these costs from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Virginia legislature, residential and small business ratepayers, NCEL (National Caucus of Environmental Legislators).
news_headline: Virginia shifts data center energy costs
news_summary: New legislation requires facilities using 25 MW or more to pay for increased generating capacity. This prevents these costs from being passed on to other customers.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Reporting
short_summary: This legislation mandates water utilities to report monthly water consumption by data centers, providing critical data for water resource management and transparency.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan (D–Loudoun), Virginia Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ), community advocates, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
opponents: Not explicitly stated (potentially some in the data center industry).
news_headline: New regulations beef up data center water reporting
news_summary: This bill mandates water utilities to report monthly water consumption by data centers. This provides critical data for water resource management and transparency.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting, Noise
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental and historical impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Community advocates, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Del. Joshua E. Thomas, Del. Sam Rasoul, Sen. Danica A. Roem.
opponents: Not explicitly stated (potentially some in the data center industry).
news_headline: Virginia's new data center siting law explained
news_summary: The law requires site assessments for noise impacts on homes and schools near new data centers. Localities can also assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
